evidence.observation: "Use a read-only engine transaction." The plan states read-only execution as a binding design rule, and §4 names the DB2 deliverable "Read-only relation bindings".

evidence.location: §4 Obligations and completion criteria, DB2 row
evidence.observation: Exit criterion: "Bind named fact roles to a read-only DuckDB snapshot and check uniqueness, inclusion and mandatory participation. Specify duplicate, NULL and type handling; include snapshot and projection identity." Nothing in it observes the read-only property itself.

evidence.location: §9 Verification and baseline, DB2 acceptance pair
evidence.observation: "DB2: introduce a duplicate in a read-only database snapshot and compare against a checked materialized population from the same rows; also test missing projection, NULL, duplicate input and incompatible type." Every case exercises verdict semantics; none exercises the read-only guarantee (no write attempt through the binding observed to fail, no before/after byte or mutation check on the database file, no refusal of a read-write connection or of a non-snapshot handle).

concerns.recommendation: Add an observable read-only gate to DB2's exit criterion and §9 acceptance pair: e.g. attempt a mutating statement through the bound connection and record the engine's refusal, and/or assert the snapshot file is byte-identical after checking; also state whether a caller-supplied read-write connection is refused or re-opened read-only.
concerns.title: DB2's defining read-only property has no observable exit gate

evidence.observation: "Bound counterexample rows independently of scan size." Stated as binding, but no bound value, home, or triggering behavior is given anywhere in the plan.
"Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." This recording obligation is not wired into any §4 exit criterion or §9 acceptance pair.

evidence.location: §4 DB3 row and §9 DB3 acceptance pair
evidence.observation: DB3 requires "Compare native and database verdicts over the same records, including missing tables, uncovered roles and bounded source keys" and §9 requires "Compare verdict, affected binding and coverage". If the database side bounds exposed counterexample bindings while native gnd check exposes them unbounded (or bounded differently), the "affected binding" comparison is under-specified; no gate constructs an over-bound input on either side.

concerns.recommendation: State the counterexample bound (value and defining component) in the plan or delegate it explicitly to a named phase decision, and add an acceptance case that exceeds the bound and records the truncated result and work counters on both the native and database sides, so DB3's binding-level parity comparison is decidable.
concerns.title: Counterexample-row bound and work counters are binding rules with no gate and no stated value

evidence.observation: "Compile a guarded existential over a joint assignment and expose violating antecedent bindings." The plan never states the connectivity rule for that joint assignment: whether consequent atoms that share no variable with each other or with the antecedent (a cross join inside the existential) are refused or supported.

§1: "The [predecessor close](../../pyrel-rules-coverage/007-milestone-close.md) records the inherited capability and the limits of its evidence." §4: "Carry the predecessor's documented limits into each new public claim." That close records a blocking panel concern, "the LQP version's exit on an empty disconnected join", squarely in this construct class; the existing exporter refuses a disconnected antecedent by name (src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py:401-403) but the plan sets no corresponding rule for the consequent join.

Acceptance fixtures "Vary identifiers, declaration order and input cardinality" — connectivity of the joint assignment is not among the varied dimensions, so the unaddressed class would also escape the fixtures.

concerns.recommendation: State in the plan (and DB1 spec) whether a disconnected existential consequent is refused by name, mirroring the antecedent rule, or compiled with defined semantics; add a disconnected-join fixture to the acceptance set so the predecessor's blocking limit is demonstrably carried forward.
concerns.title: Connectivity rule for the existential join is unstated despite a predecessor blocking limit in this class

evidence.observation: "Compile a guarded existential over a joint assignment and expose violating antecedent bindings." The plan describes one compilation without naming its target; the starting exporter renders two programs from one requirement list (src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py:7-19, TARGETS = ("duckdb", "lqp") at :48), and the DB1 spec's design retains only `--rules duckdb`.

"Other SQL engines and general SQL compilation." LQP is not another SQL engine; it is the same exporter's second target, which today refuses what it cannot enforce locally (e.g. vacuity, pyrel_rules.py:2739). The plan leaves undefined whether `--rules lqp` gains the existential consequent, refuses it by name, or silently shares the new requirement.

concerns.recommendation: Add one sentence to §2 or §4 stating the LQP disposition for the new consequent kind (support, named refusal, or explicit deferral with a tracked issue), since DB1 changes a public two-target interface.
concerns.title: LQP target disposition for the new existential fragment is undefined

evidence.observation: "Its November 27 review flagged 105 descriptions older than their source; resolve contract details against code and tests." The repository's copy of that review, dev/components/REVIEW.md:154, reports the group as "Descriptions older than their code (not computed: the catalog has no git history here) (0)"; the 105 figure appears only as boilerplate repeated across sibling milestone plans and is not derivable from the checked-in artifact.

concerns.recommendation: Either cite the review run that produced 105 (with its evidence path) or restate §3 against the checked-in review, which currently reports that group as not computed with count 0, so the premise for resolving contract details against code is verifiable.
concerns.title: Cited count of 105 stale component descriptions is not borne out by the checked-in review

summary: Digest matched. Reviewed the DuckDB rule-checking plan against the rubric (DuckDB lowering, native differential behavior, safety and resource controls vs plan gates), with the DB1 spec, predecessor close, exporter source, api.check input validation and the component-index review as context. Baseline intake claims verified plausible (existential consequent refused at pyrel_rules.py:400, non-Population/path population rejected at api.py:260-262). Two blocking gate gaps: the DB2 deliverable's defining read-only property and the §0/§6 resource controls have no observable exit criterion or acceptance pair, leaving the plan's own binding rules undemonstrated at closure; plus hardening gaps on existential-join connectivity (a predecessor blocking limit) and the LQP target's disposition. Issue texts #327/#330 were not fetchable in this review mode, so issue conformance was assessed through the plan's own restatement.
